notes: Derived from SA-1 fixture checkov-ec2-ckv-aws-289-23890 + remediation_package #2482.

remediation_steps.step:
Back up the current Terraform file to ensure changes can be reverted if necessary.

Command:
    cp /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

Why: Creating a backup allows for easy rollback in case the changes need to be reverted.

Modify the IAM policy to restrict permissions by implementing least privilege principles.

Command:
    sed -i 's/"Action": "s3:GetObject"/"Action": "s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject"/' /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf

Why: Restricting permissions to specific actions and resources reduces the risk of unauthorized access and aligns with security best practices.

Plan the Terraform changes to ensure the modifications are correct and will be applied as expected.

Command:
    cd /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode

Why: Running a plan allows you to verify that the changes are correct and will not cause any unexpected issues.

Apply the Terraform changes to enforce the updated IAM policy.

Command:
    terraform apply -auto-approve

Why: Applying the changes updates the IAM policy to enforce the least privilege principle, reducing security risks.

Verify the IAM policy changes by checking the policy document.

Command:
    aws iam get-policy-version --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/vulnerable_policy --version-id v1

Why: Verifying the policy ensures that the changes have been applied correctly and the policy now adheres to least privilege principles.
remediation_steps.source: AWS Security Best Practices in IAM

remediation_steps.step:
Re-scan with Checkov to confirm CKV_AWS_289 no longer fails.

Command:
    checkov -d /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab --check CKV_AWS_289 --output json --quiet --compact

Why: Re-scanning with Checkov verifies that the vulnerability has been remediated according to the scanner's criteria.
